Daniel has been a staple in the Australian music community, on drums for bands Lower Plenty and Deaf Wish , the mind behind the music of beloved duo Hot Tubs Time Machine , as a member of experimental groups Vision200 and iceclaw, or as a part-time guest with many including Nathan Roche, Talk Show, Summer Flake, Lily Morris, LOU, Brickhead and more. In all of these acts, Daniel has played a supporting role. A quiet contributor. While he wouldn’t describe this project as a step into the limelight, it does mark a step out on his own. This is his first solo album recorded and mixed at home by Daniel, starting in Oct 2018 and finished in May this year. Pulling from references Arthur Russell, The Go-Betweens and the quieter moments of Yo La Tengo. The music is beautiful and layered, subtle and quiet. Not a bold statement about individuality, rather an invitation to step into the artists’ quiet thoughts. The instrumentation reflects this fragile place. Tender loops made on nylon string guitar feature on most of the songs on the album. Over the top of this Twomey layers woody and spacious clarinet, gentle percussion and subtle, almost shy, vocal harmonies. Thematically, the album explores the stepping off point between relationships ending - friendships, bands, family ties - and finding yourself alone. It is a fragile space that hovers between the pain of loss and the thrum of new opportunities. This is an album that invites you in. A catalogue of subtle shifts. An artist parting company. A shift away from the comforts of collaboration. A first step out on one’s own - albeit a tentative one. Support Dissent! In celebration of his fourth studio album, Felipe Baldomir is heading out on his biggest world tour yet, with dates across Australia, New Zealand, Europe, the UK, South Africa and South America throughout 2026–2027. Beach Day (November 6, 2026) is a feel-good collection of songs inspired by life on the Australian coastline. It has a sound of its own — it’s upbeat, indie, fresh and just a lot of fun. As a multi-instrumentalist and live-looping artist, Felipe layers groovy guitar riffs, drums, keys, synths and saxophone to create a dynamic, full-band sound while performing solo. The new album is also being released alongside a Beach Day Art Collection, created by Felipe as another way to bring the world of the record to life and elevate the listening experience. Born in Uruguay and now based in Byron Bay, Australia, Felipe’s music reflects a life shaped by different coastlines, cultures and communities. What started with busking, van life and backyard shows has grown over the years into sold-out headline shows and festival stages around the world — all built independently, one show at a time. The Beach Day World Tour marks the biggest chapter yet for the coastal indie-folk singer-songwriter. “The dream for me has always been to take the music to all corners of the world, connect with like-minded people and experience new cultures wherever the music takes me.” A new album, a new show and a whole lot of new places to go.
